local.h: Illinois House could elect its first woman speaker
local.b: Five women lawmakers are among the names floated to succeed Speaker Emanuel "Chris" Welch, who will not seek a fourth term as speaker.
local.title: Will the Illinois House elect its first woman speaker? Dems float potential contenders to replace Welch

local.h: Chicago Democrats rally in the Loop after midterm wins
local.b: More than 100 supporters gathered at Federal Plaza on Saturday. Representative-elect Daniel Biss told them, "Y'all did your job, and now it's time for people like me to do our job."
local.title: After Democrats won big during midterm election, Chicago supporters rally for 'productive change'

local.h: Chicago parking attendants reach deal to end strike
local.b: Teamsters Local 727 reached a tentative agreement Friday with the Chicago Parking Association after a strike that began Tuesday at O'Hare, McCormick Place and the Hyatt Regency. The union has nearly 1,200 members.
local.title: Chicago parking attendants reach deal with operators to end strike

local.h: Chicago businesses brace for state hemp ban
local.b: THC drinks grew to nearly half of Marz Brewing's production, and its founder says they 'truly rescued our business.'
local.title: How Chicago businesses are bracing for the state's hemp ban

local.h: California voters reject Prop. 45 environmental review changes
local.b: With about 76% of votes counted, the measure to fast-track reviews under the California Environmental Quality Act was failing 55.7% to 44.3%.
local.title: Californians vote to keep environmental protections, even with the red tape

local.h: Long Beach cancels Naples Island Holiday Boat Parade
local.b: Organizers called off the tradition, held since 1946, because expected high tides and heavy surf would make it unsafe. It is the first cancellation in six years for an event that draws about 60,000 spectators.
local.title: Naples Boat Parade canceled as El Niño season threatens dangerously high tides over Christmas week

local.h: Boyle Heights rally denounces ICE activity at White Memorial
local.b: Crowds marched to Adventist Health White Memorial after federal immigration agents blockaded the emergency room entrance and detained at least two people. State Sen. Maria Elena Durazo called the agents' actions at the hospital unacceptable.
local.title: Community, LA leaders denounce ICE activity at White Memorial

local.h: ICE detains two US citizens protesting at hospital
local.b: Rapid response groups say the protest outside White Memorial Hospital began after people saw someone detained and taken inside.
local.title: ICE detains two US citizens protesting outside White Memorial Hospital, rapid response groups say

goodnews.h: LAUSD coffee cake becomes a wedding cake
goodnews.b: Valley native Micki Boden served the LAUSD coffee cake she ate from kindergarten through high school at her October wedding.
goodnews.title: How LAUSD’s famed coffee cake became this Valley bride’s wedding cake

local.h: New York sends 20 Democrats and 6 Republicans to the House
local.b: Democrat Cait Conley flipped the Hudson Valley's 17th District by defeating Rep. Mike Lawler. Rep. Nicole Malliotakis remains the city's only Republican in Congress.
local.title: New York’s House delegation will include 20 Democrats and six Republicans

local.h: Woman dies after falling from moving SUV on the BQE
local.b: Police said the 37-year-old opened a rear door and fell out near the Brooklyn Bridge around 2:30 a.m. Sunday, then was struck by another car. No arrests have been made.
local.title: Brooklyn woman killed after tumbling from a moving SUV on the BQE near Brooklyn Bridge

local.h: Judge orders NYC to give ICE names of Bronx shelter residents
local.b: Judge Lewis Kaplan ruled the city must comply with the subpoena. City Hall, which bars agencies from cooperating with ICE, had fought it.
local.title: Federal judge rules Mamdani administration must give ICE names of Bronx shelter residents

local.h: Work begins to replace Newark Bay Bridge
local.b: The 1956 span carries about 95,000 vehicles a day. The new bridge is due in 2031 and the old one stays open meanwhile.
local.title: Work is underway to replace deteriorating Newark Bay Bridge, a major NY-NJ route

local.h: Schools employee charged in Brooklyn jogger's murder
local.b: Police charged Sayed Mohassib, 27, in the Oct. 30 stabbing of Katie Suarez on the Shore Parkway path. He has been suspended.
local.title: NYPD arrests and charges city schools employee in murder of Brooklyn jogger

local.h: Quest pays $13M over Giants ticket kickbacks
local.b: Prosecutors say the lab company offered clients suite seats and training camp access in exchange for referrals.
local.title: Quest Diagnostics pays $13M to settle kickback allegations involving NY Giants tickets

goodnews.h: Mamdani expands free produce programs for SNAP recipients
goodnews.b: The city is adding funding to Health Bucks and Get the Good Stuff, which matches SNAP spending on fresh or frozen fruits, vegetables and beans dollar for dollar.
goodnews.title: Mamdani expands free produce programs for New Yorkers on SNAP

local.h: France investigates whether foreign powers sent airline bomb threats
local.b: Paris prosecutors opened a probe into hoax bomb threats against dozens of flights in Europe over the past week. No explosives have been found.
local.title: France probes if bomb threats against airlines linked to 'foreign powers'

local.h: Clashes in Paris as cost-of-living protests enter fourth weekend
local.b: The interior ministry counted 146,000 protesters across France on Saturday, including 46,000 in Paris, fewer than in previous weeks. Police used tear gas at the end of the Paris march against people throwing projectiles and fireworks.
local.title: Clashes in Paris after new French protests

local.h: France marks Armistice Day on Wednesday
local.b: Nov. 11 is a public holiday, with parades and wreaths at war memorials and the President laying a wreath at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at the Arc de Triomphe. Paris Photo opens Thursday.
local.title: On the Agenda: What's happening in France this week

local.h: Students and teachers call new strike for Tuesday
local.b: Groups say the government is 'starting to yield' and want to broaden the protest movement.

local.h: AFP denounces police violence against reporters
local.b: An AFP photographer wearing a press armband suffered a broken leg from baton blows during a police charge in Lyon.

local.h: Yellow Vests plan banned Paris rally
local.b: Unions and students hold an authorised march against the high cost of living, while the Yellow Vests call a separate rally at Place de la Concorde despite a ban.
